text:
maria_s: Hey team, customer on Private VPC says model pulls and health pings are failing after they enabled strict egress rules. Getting TLS handshake errors and DNS NXDOMAIN for model registry + telemetry. Can we get a minimal egress checklist?

kevin_support: Thanks Maria. Any error snippets from their side? Are they seeing auth 401s or TLS cert mismatch?

maria_s: TLS errors in our gateway logs: 
```
tls: handshake failure: tls: oversized_record_received
remote: x.x.x.x:443
```
Also their node logs show: `getaddrinfo models-registry.redwood.ai: Name or service not known`.

sasha_sre: Sounds like either DNS resolution to our registry is blocked or there's an intercepting proxy doing TLS inspection (SNI rewrite). For allowlist we typically need:
- DNS to resolve `*.redwood.ai` and `models-registry.redwood.ai`
- HTTPS to `registry.redwood.ai`, `auth.redwood.ai`, `telemetry.redwood.ai` on 443
- OCSP/responder endpoints (for cert revocation checks) e.g., `ocsp.digicert.com` and `crl.*` (443/80 as needed)
- Package repos: `pypi.org`, `files.pythonhosted.org`, `deb.debian.org`, `archive.ubuntu.com` (443/80) for onprem bootstrap

kevin_support: Adding to that: OAuth endpoints `accounts.redwood.ai` and `login.redwood.ai` for token exchange, and `s3.redwood-internal` for model artifacts if they're using S3-backed registry. Also allow outbound to our telemetry endpoints `telemetry.redwood.ai/api/v1` (443).

maria_s: Customer is air-gapped-ish and only whitelisted hosts. They asked for a one-shot curl to reproduce. I gave them: 
```
curl -v https://models-registry.redwood.ai/v1/health
```
They get `curl: (56) SSL_read: errno 0` which lines up with TLS interception.

alex_cs: From CS side, customer ran an enterprise proxy that performs TLS MITM with a local root CA. If SNI passthrough is required we advise them to allow raw TCP 443 to the above hosts or install our root CA in their proxy? Prefer passthrough for security.

sasha_sre: Also check DNS resolution path: some onprem DNS forwards to internal recursive resolvers that strip EDNS or return NXDOMAIN for unknown external suffixes. Ask them to run: 
```
dig +short models-registry.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
traceroute -T -p 443 models-registry.redwood.ai
```
If `dig` to 8.8.8.8 resolves but internal resolver doesn't, they need to allow DNS traffic to public resolvers or add split-horizon rules.

kevin_support: For firewall rules we suggest allowing outbound TCP 443 to the following hostnames (minimal):
- models-registry.redwood.ai
- registry.redwood.ai
- auth.redwood.ai
- telemetry.redwood.ai
- accounts.redwood.ai
- files.pythonhosted.org
- pypi.org
- s3.amazonaws.com (if S3 registry)
Ports: 80, 443. Also allow UDP 53 for DNS or allow DNS-over-TLS/HTTPS to specific resolvers if using DoT/DoH.

maria_s: Customer added `models-registry.redwood.ai` and `auth.redwood.ai` but still failing. I asked for a packet capture — they reported seeing a proxy rewrite cert with CN=Corporate-Proxy.

sasha_sre: That's the root cause then. Either: 1) Enable SNI passthrough for those hosts on the proxy, or 2) Install corporate root CA in the container JVM/truststore (not ideal). Also ensure OCSP is allowed: some CAs do online revocation checks to `ocsp.*` which if blocked can cause handshake delays/failures.

alex_cs: Customer opted for SNI passthrough. They opened a ticket with their network team to add TCP passthrough for `models-registry.redwood.ai` and `auth.redwood.ai` and allow outbound UDP 53 to 8.8.8.8.

deploy-bot: deploy status: no impacted services on our side. :white_check_mark:

kevin_support: Once they confirm, run the test again: 
```
curl -v https://models-registry.redwood.ai/v1/health --resolve models-registry.redwood.ai:443:<resolved-ip>
```
And check `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername models-registry.redwood.ai` to confirm cert CN is from Redwood CA.

maria_s: Customer reported back "green" after passthrough change. Health endpoints and model pulls working. They still want a short KB for onprem teams about common egress hosts and TLS inspection notes. Can someone draft a small checklist we can link in the support KB? :eyes: 

sasha_sre: I'll draft a checklist and include commands + minimal host list + OCSP/CRL notes. Will link to internal KB once done.

alex_cs: Thanks everyone — closing the loop with the customer and will add the KB link in the ticket. :thumbsup:
